To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified several phosphorylation sites on homomeric and on heteromeric TRMPM6 and TRPM6, and that we have found that S1565, a site that is conserved in all TRPM channels, is a potential regulatory site that is transphosphorylable from TRPM6 to TRPM7 and that is predicted to affect the catalytic activity of TRPM7 by influencing the access of substrate into the active site pocket of the channel-kinase.

we identified phosphorylation sites in both TRPM7 and in TRPM6 and that phosphorylation of TRPM6’s S1565 residue in TRPM7 is predicted to structrually affect TRPM7's functionally conserved catalytic N/D loop.

we used mass spectrometry to identify phosphorylation sites on the bifunctional channel-kinases, TRPM6 and/or TRPM7, and then we conducted site-directed mutagenesis to determine the functional significance of several of the sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of TRPM7 and, in part, TRPM6 phosphorylated amino acid residues and their functional significance.
the identification and functional analysis of TRPM6- and TRPM7-specific phosphorylation sites and how these sites regulate the channel-kinase activity of TRPM6/7.
the identification and functional characterization of TRPM7 and, to a lesser degree, TRPM6 phosphorylated sites and their role in channel function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mass spectrometric analyses of TRPM7 and the TRPM7/6 channel-kinase complex have identified numerous sites that are phosphorylated by TRPM7 or TRPM6.
the present study identified phosphorylation sites and regulatory mechanisms of the channel kinases TRPM6 and/or TRPM7.
our study provides the first mass spectrometric identification of the TRPM7/6 phosphorylation sites and that we identified a potential regulatory mechanism for TRPM7 kinase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPM6 and -7 are regulated through phosphorylation of multiple sites, and that TRPM7 kinase activity is controlled through phosphorylation of S1777 and S1565.
TRPM7’s kinase activity is regulated by phosphorylation of both the catalytic and exchange domains.
TRPM6 and 7 are phosphorylated at many sites that are likely involved in the regulation of the channel-kinase activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TRPM6 and -7 channels are highly phosphorylated and phosphorylation is an important regulatory mechanism of the channel-kinases.
phosphorylation is an important regulatory mechanism for TRPM7, and that phosphorylation of TRPM6 can also regulate TRPM7 activity.

phosphorylation of TRPM7 and its transphosphorylational modification by TRPM6 is a highly dynamic process, with numerous phosphorylation sites that may function in the regulation of channel-kinase activity.
